reasons: Attempt 8 is the most mergeable of the candidates. Its many-alternative fast path is the only one that both avoids the per-call O(n) scan and refuses to enter the shortcut when an alternative carries a parse action or results name, has its own ignore expression, or differs in whitespace handling. Attempts 2 and 5 build their lookup for the same large benefit but do not exclude alternatives with parse actions; in MatchFirst that changes error handling for a matching alternative whose action fails, and in Or it can bypass the careful exception collection. Attempt 3 is safer there, but it stores a bound parseImpl on each instance, which needs copy-time cleanup, and its Or fast path still runs `all(e.callPreparse for e in self.exprs)` on every hit, leaving the many-alternative Or case at 33x instead of the 200x plus the other candidates reach. Attempt 8 combines the stricter eligibility checks with cached `_all_call_preparse`, falls back to the original loop on any lookup miss, recomputes the lookup on ParseExpression.copy, and applies the small ParseResults and _parseNoCache/_parseCache savings only where they are semantically equivalent. That is the trade a maintainer is most likely to accept given the measured results.
